BYD Introduces M9 to Australia, the Large and Luxurious Minivan Has the DM-i Dual Mode 5.0 SH Setup
46 photos
Photo: BYD
China's BYD , the world's top electric carmaker, has an important presence in Australia and recently introduced its new energy people mover to the market to offer even more choice across the lineup – starting from AU $61,990 without on-road costs, or a little over $41k at the current exchange rate.
BYD is making its presence felt as much as possible just about everywhere, including the Land Down Under. They say that models like the Sealion 7 benefit the people who need them the most, including in rural areas; they joined forces earlier this month with the AFL (Australian Football League) by signing a major partnership with the Hawthorn Football Club, and back in October already celebrated 150k unit sales in the region.
As far as models are concerned, BYD made available in September the smaller ATTO 2 DM-i featuring the Dual Mode 4.0 Super Hybrid platform and the Blade battery using Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) chemistry, as well as the ATTO 3 featuring the new e-Platform 3.0 EV architecture with 800 volts.
Now it’s time for a proper flagship of the people mover variety – the company first confirmed the all-new BYD M9 minivan was coming to Australia back in August and then announced the pricing configuration in September, with the model starting from AU $61,990 for the base eight-seat M9 Dynamic model and from AU $72,990 (over $48k) sans OTR for the seven-seat M9 Premium variant.
The Chinese brand now announces the arrival of the BYD M9 on the market, with BYD's first new energy people mover bringing together the “brand's expertise in new energy vehicle mobility with the versatility Australians expect from large and well-appointed mobility.” Initially, the first version touching down in the Land Down Under is the top-spec seven-seat Premium grade, featuring a 2+2+3 configuration with luxurious leather-appointed and second-row captain’s chairs, a 15.6-inch rear entertainment screen and a 12-speaker audio system among the highlights.
The more versatile eight-seat M9 Dynamic featuring a 2+3+3 seating arrangement will come before the end of the year, and both share the latest DM-i Dual Mode 5.0 Super Hybrid system, three-zone air-conditioning, and 470 liters (16.59 cu. Ft.) for luggage with all seats raised. With the rear seats folded, the M9 has 2,036 liters of space – or 71.9 cubic feet of storage.
The Dynamic grade has Frequency Selective Damping technology, while the Premium gets BYD's DiSus-C Intelligent Damping Body Control system, but the intelligent plug-in hybrid system is common to both. It consists of a 1.5-liter turbocharged Xiaoyun gasoline engine and a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor with a combined output of 191kW for Dynamic and 218kW for Premium – that’s 256 hp or 292 horsepower.
The Dynamic features a 20.4kWh BYD Blade Battery offering up to 80 km of pure electric range or 50 miles, while the Premium version is even more capable thanks to its larger 36.6kWh battery – EV range soars to 145 km or 90 miles. Total combined range is 790km and 850km, respectively, based on WLTP – or 491 and 528 miles, respectively.
Both the M9 Dynamic and Premium are solely available with front-wheel drive, though, and feature three intelligent operating modes: EV Pure Electric, HEV Series, where the gasoline engine only acts as a power generator, and HEV Parallel, where both the gasoline and electric motor work together. Inside, BYD gives the driver a 12.3-inch digital instrument display and a 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
